findings.highlight: You don't really think of it as anything special yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が偉いわけじゃないのに、自慢するのって、おかしいよね
findings.explanation: Setsuna calls it odd for her to boast because she herself is not the person whose achievement makes Haruki admirable. The English says Haruki does not regard his own behavior as special, transferring her self-effacing concern to his self-evaluation.
findings.japanese:
『なんてね。
自分が偉いわけじゃないのに、
自慢するのって、おかしいよね…』
findings.todokanai: "Just kidding. You don't really think of it as anything special yourself, so me being proud sounds kinda weird, doesn't it…?"

findings.highlight: I'll text you again after your paper's done.
findings.evidenceJa: レポート終わったらまたメールしてね
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks Haruki to email her once the paper is finished. The English says she will text him again afterward, reversing who is expected to initiate the completion report and weakening her request for continued contact.
findings.japanese:
『それじゃ、頑張って。
レポート終わったらまたメールしてね』
findings.todokanai: "Anyway, I'll be cheering you on. I'll text you again after your paper's done."

findings.highlight: "I think both suit you just fine."
findings.evidenceJa: 「どっちも充足するっちゃぁするだろ」
findings.explanation: Haruki says the toilet could satisfy either proposed urge, while the English says both options suit Chiaki.
findings.japanese: 「どっちも充足するっちゃぁするだろ」
findings.todokanai: "I think both suit you just fine."

findings.highlight: Are you that interested in me?
findings.evidenceJa: 惚れた弱みって言うか
findings.explanation: Chiaki explicitly teases that Haruki's knowledge of her may be the weakness of having fallen in love. The English reduces this to mere interest, removing the romantic proposition Haruki is being baited to confront.
findings.japanese:
「やだな～もう。
どこまであたしのことわかっちゃってんのよ春希～。
もうなんての？　惚れた弱みって言うか？」
findings.todokanai: "Oh, come on～! You know so much about me already, Haruki～ What's this? Are you that interested in me?"

findings.highlight: report the progress of my paper
findings.evidenceJa: レポートの顛末は、日付が変わる前に伝えないと
findings.explanation: Haruki must report how Chiaki's paper turned out before midnight because Setsuna is waiting for news. The English calls it his paper, erasing the very reason he has lied about still working and obscuring the betrayal he recognizes in the next lines.
findings.japanese:
『あまり遅くまで待つな』って
前のメールに書いてしまった以上、
レポートの顛末は、日付が変わる前に伝えないと。
findings.todokanai: Since I told her to not stay up too late, I should at least report the progress of my paper to her before the date changes.

findings.highlight: Every time we get together, they start arguing
findings.evidenceJa: 親同士がさ、あたしの目の前で、顔を合わせるたびキッツい喧嘩をしてた時は
findings.explanation: Chiaki recalls the period when her parents fought whenever they met and says she also sympathized with this side—her mother. The English makes the fights present and recurring whenever “we” meet, then says she sometimes feels sorry for both parents, changing time and referent.
findings.japanese:
「親同士がさ、あたしの目の前で、
顔を合わせるたびキッツい喧嘩をしてた時は、
そりゃ、嫌な気分だったけど、こっち側に同情もしてた」
findings.todokanai: "Every time we get together, they start arguing like crazy right in front of my eyes. It does get annoying, but sometimes I actually feel sorry for them."

findings.highlight: When will I finally be able to put those broken fragments of my memories back together again, I wonder…?
findings.evidenceJa:
あの時に散らばってしまった想いの欠片、
いつか拾い集めること、できるんだろうか…
findings.explanation: Fragments of feelings scattered three years ago become fragments of memories.
findings.japanese:
あの時に散らばってしまった想いの欠片、
いつか拾い集めること、できるんだろうか…
findings.todokanai: When will I finally be able to put those broken fragments of my memories back together again, I wonder…?

findings.evidenceJa: 『貴重な無駄だったね』という一言を、俺はいつか、実感することができるのかな
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether he will someday be able to feel the truth of Chiaki's smiling description, “a valuable waste.” The English declares her words utterly superficial, inventing a dismissive judgment that reverses his tentative hope of understanding them.
findings.japanese:
別れ際、あいつがにっこりと笑って言った
『貴重な無駄だったね』という一言を、
俺はいつか、実感することができるのかな。
findings.todokanai: Her cheerful parting words of "what a valuable waste of time that was" felt utterly superficial. I wonder if I'll ever be able to feel the same way?

findings.highlight: You sent me a text yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 昨日着信くれたでしょ
findings.explanation: Chiaki returns a call her mother placed yesterday; 着信 denotes the incoming or missed call. The English says her mother sent a text, changing the communication event as their relationship begins to soften.
findings.japanese:
「あ、母さん？
昨日着信くれたでしょ？　何？」
findings.todokanai: "Hey, Mom? You sent me a text yesterday, right? What's up?"

findings.highlight: "Ah, my brother yelled at me just now. I guess it's a bad idea to light a few celebratory firecrackers when it's already past midnight."
findings.evidenceJa:
『あ、今、弟に怒鳴られちゃった。
０時過ぎにクラッカーはまずかったみたい』
findings.explanation: A celebratory party popper becomes several firecrackers.
findings.japanese:
『あ、今、弟に怒鳴られちゃった。
０時過ぎにクラッカーはまずかったみたい』
findings.todokanai: "Ah, my brother yelled at me just now. I guess it's a bad idea to light a few celebratory firecrackers when it's already past midnight."

findings.highlight: I don't have an answer to that question
findings.evidenceJa: 質問に対する返答がまだ
findings.explanation: Drunk Setsuna tells “Professor” Haruki that his response to her question is still missing. The English says she herself lacks an answer, reversing who owes whom a reply in their flirtatious exchange about his winter plans.
findings.japanese:
『せんせ～
質問に対する返答がまだで～す』
findings.todokanai: "Sorry, Professor～! I don't have an answer to that question yeeet～"
